## The problem

Job seekers in analytics see thousands of postings but very little structure:
which roles pay more, which skills matter and where the jobs actually are. Our
team set out to build a site that answers those questions for one industry,
Computer Systems Design and Related Services (NAICS 5415).

## What I did

- Built the data pipeline that filters a 504,208-row job postings extract down
  to a clean, 12-month panel of 1,790 postings for NAICS 5415.
- Wrote the location and salary cleaning scripts, including a fix for
  Washington, DC postings that were being counted as Washington State.
- Added role family and years of experience fields so the team could compare
  roles side by side.
- Proposed switching industries after finding that our first choice,
  pharmaceutical manufacturing, had only 39 postings in the data.
- Wrote the literature review that frames why the project matters.

## Results

The pipeline gives the team one consistent dataset that every page of the site
draws from, and the numbers in the text are computed from the data instead of
typed in by hand.

## What I learned

Most of the work in a data product happens before the first chart. Small
cleaning decisions, like how to read a location field, can quietly change every
number downstream, so I now check edge cases early and write down every rule I
apply.
